Adjusted earnings in its fiscal second quarter, which concludes at the end of November, will surpass the $4.05 a share the courier generated last year, Chief Financial Officer John Dietrich told investors Tuesday at an industry conference. Analysts are anticipating $4.02 a share on average in estimates compiled by Bloomberg.

The comments sent FedEx shares up 5.3% as of 1:38 p.m. in New York. Rival United Parcel Service Inc. climbed as well.

“What you’re seeing right now clearly is something of a relief rally when people have been pretty negative on the prospects for both FedEx and UPS,” said Ari Rosa, an analyst at Citigroup Inc. “That reflects a lot of challenges that these companies have faced over the last 12 to 24 months.”

The package-delivery industry has been grappling with uncertain demand ahead of the peak-shipping season and rising costs from President Donald Trump’s tariffs. FedEx and UPS are also expected to encounter disruptions and higher expenses from the grounding of their MD-11 aircraft following the fatal crash last week of a UPS freighter.

The grounding could be more of a burden for UPS, with the plane type accounting for about 9% of its total fleet, according to filings. The MD-11 represents about 4% of FedEx’s fleet.

The latest developments are pushing the couriers to turn to third-party charters to maintain operations, writes Brian Ossenbeck, an analyst at JP Morgan Securities. The outsourcing is likely to lead to higher costs for the companies, especially as increased demand could push up air freight rates.

“Protecting service during peak comes at a cost,” Ossenbeck wrote in a note.

# FedEx Corp. Board Declares Quarterly Dividend

Business Wire

1 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

+1.33%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

**MEMPHIS, Tenn., November 21, 2025**--([BUSINESS WIRE](https://www.businesswire.com))--The Board of Directors of FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) today declared a quarterly cash dividend of $1.45 per share on FedEx Corp. common stock, in line with the company’s continued focus on delivering stockholder value. The dividend is payable January 6, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 15, 2025.

FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce and business services. With annual revenue of $89 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. Consistently ranked among the world’s most admired and trusted employers, FedEx inspires its more than 500,000 employees to remain focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards and the needs of their customers and communities. FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040. To learn more, please visit [fedex.com/about](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fedex.com%2Fabout&esheet=54361455&newsitemid=20251120544592&lan=en-US&anchor=fedex.com%2Fabout&index=1&md5=02881aabeb07dba5a31e603b10e2ff60).

# Is FedEx Stock Underperforming the Nasdaq?

Sohini Mondal

2 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.85%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

[^IXIC

-0.38%](/quote/%5EIXIC/ "^IXIC")

With a market cap of $65 billion, FedEx Corporation (FDX) is a global provider of transportation, e-commerce, and business services operating through its Federal Express and FedEx Freight segments. The company offers a wide range of shipping, logistics, printing, and digital solutions to support businesses and consumers worldwide.

Companies valued at $10 billion or more are generally considered "large-cap" stocks, and FedEx fits this criterion. FedEx has grown into a leading player in express delivery and supply chain management.

Shares of the Memphis, Tennessee-based company have declined 9.4% from its 52-week high of $302.02. FDX stock has soared 18.5% over the past three months, outperforming the Nasdaq Composite’s ($NASX) 7.7% gain over the same time frame.

In the longer term, FDX stock is down 2.7% on a YTD basis, lagging behind NASX’s 21% gain. Moreover, shares of the company have decreased 9.6% over the past 52 weeks, compared to NASX’s 22.6% return over the same time frame.

Despite a few fluctuations, the stock has been trading above its 50-day moving average since June.

Shares of FDX rose 2.3% following its Q1 2026 results on Sep. 18 because the company posted solid year-over-year earnings growth, with adjusted operating income increasing to $1.30 billion and adjusted EPS rising to $3.83, driven by strong U.S. domestic package revenue and structural cost reductions. Investors were also encouraged by FedEx’s fiscal 2026 outlook, including 4% - 6% revenue growth and $17.20 - $19 adjusted EPS after excluding optimization, spin-off, and fiscal-year-change costs.

Additionally, confidence improved due to FedEx completing $500 million in share repurchases during the quarter and advancing toward the planned June 2026 spin-off of FedEx Freight.

In contrast, rival United Parcel Service, Inc. (UPS) has lagged behind FDX stock. Shares of United Parcel Service have dipped 24.3% on a YTD basis and 29.6% over the past 52 weeks.

Despite the stock’s underperformance over the past year, analysts remain moderately optimistic on FedEx. The stock has a consensus rating of “Moderate Buy” from 30 analysts in coverage, and as of writing, it is trading above the mean price target of $268.52.

# FedEx Climbs as Profit Guidance Eases Holiday Season Worries

Cailley LaPara and Matthew Griffin

2 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.05%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

[UPS

+0.13%](/quote/UPS/ "UPS")

(Bloomberg) -- FedEx Corp. expects profit this quarter to improve from a year ago, easing investor concerns about a lackluster holiday season and volatile trade policies.

Most Read from Bloomberg

* [Will the YIMBY ‘Holy Grail’ Deliver an LA Building Boom?](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2025-11-11/los-angeles-preps-for-building-boom-after-yimby-housing-reforms?utm_campaign=bn&utm_medium=distro&utm_source=yahooUS)
* [Jamie Dimon’s $4 Billion Fortress HQ Takes On the New York Skyline](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2025-11-10/jamie-dimon-s-4-billion-headquarters-at-270-park-avenue-overshadows-manhattan?utm_campaign=bn&utm_medium=distro&utm_source=yahooUS)

Adjusted earnings in its fiscal second quarter, which concludes at the end of November, will surpass the $4.05 a share the courier generated last year, Chief Financial Officer John Dietrich told investors Tuesday at an industry conference. Analysts are anticipating $4.02 a share on average in estimates compiled by Bloomberg.

The comments sent FedEx shares up 5.3% as of 1:38 p.m. in New York. Rival United Parcel Service Inc. climbed as well.

“What you’re seeing right now clearly is something of a relief rally when people have been pretty negative on the prospects for both FedEx and UPS,” said Ari Rosa, an analyst at Citigroup Inc. “That reflects a lot of challenges that these companies have faced over the last 12 to 24 months.”

The package-delivery industry has been grappling with uncertain demand ahead of the peak-shipping season and rising costs from President Donald Trump’s tariffs. FedEx and UPS are also expected to encounter disruptions and higher expenses from the grounding of their MD-11 aircraft following the fatal crash last week of a UPS freighter.

The grounding could be more of a burden for UPS, with the plane type accounting for about 9% of its total fleet, according to filings. The MD-11 represents about 4% of FedEx’s fleet.

The latest developments are pushing the couriers to turn to third-party charters to maintain operations, writes Brian Ossenbeck, an analyst at JP Morgan Securities. The outsourcing is likely to lead to higher costs for the companies, especially as increased demand could push up air freight rates.

“Protecting service during peak comes at a cost,” Ossenbeck wrote in a note.

# What Catalysts Are Reshaping the FedEx Story for Investors?

Simply Wall St

5 min read

Analysts have nudged their consensus price target for FedEx upward, now forecasting $271.93 from the previous $267.71. This modest increase reflects a growing optimism around FedEx’s near-term potential, supported by fresh operational improvements and encouraging earnings results. Stay tuned to discover how you can track ongoing shifts in sentiment and keep pace with the evolving story around FedEx stock.

[Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value FedEx.](https://www.simplywall.st/company/id/e8cdcdb9-2f1c-48bf-aa39-92af2e595877/valuation?utm_medium=finance_user&utm_campaign=cta_valuation_alternatives&utm_source=yahoo)

## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

## What's in the News

* FedEx is securing additional freighters after indefinitely grounding its MD-11 jet fleet. This move is intended to help manage operational complexities during the busy holiday shipping season, as reported by Bloomberg.
* At its recent Analyst and Investor Day, FedEx presented ongoing initiatives that prioritize operational improvements and maintain strict cost discipline.
* The company has updated its guidance for fiscal year 2026 and now expects revenue growth between 4 percent and 6 percent, depending on how both domestic and international markets perform.
* FedEx completed a significant share buyback, repurchasing over 2.1 million shares for nearly $500 million. This was part of a broader $3.5 billion repurchase program.

## How This Changes the Fair Value For FedEx

* The consensus analyst price target has risen slightly from $267.71 to $271.93. This reflects greater optimism around FedEx's near-term valuation.
* The discount rate increased modestly from 8.76% to 8.89%. This suggests a marginal rise in perceived risk or required returns.
* Revenue growth estimates show a negligible uptick, moving from 4.01% to 4.01% on a projected annual basis.
* Net profit margin remains virtually unchanged, easing marginally from 5.32% to 5.32%.
* The future P/E ratio edged higher from 14.36x to 14.64x. This indicates slightly elevated expectations for future earnings multiples.

**MEMPHIS, Tenn., November 21, 2025**--([BUSINESS WIRE](https://www.businesswire.com))--The Board of Directors of FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) today declared a quarterly cash dividend of $1.45 per share on FedEx Corp. common stock, in line with the company’s continued focus on delivering stockholder value. The dividend is payable January 6, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 15, 2025.

FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce and business services. With annual revenue of $89 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. Consistently ranked among the world’s most admired and trusted employers, FedEx inspires its more than 500,000 employees to remain focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards and the needs of their customers and communities. FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040. # Is FedEx Stock Underperforming the Nasdaq?

Sohini Mondal

2 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.85%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

[^IXIC

-0.38%](/quote/%5EIXIC/ "^IXIC")

With a market cap of $65 billion, FedEx Corporation (FDX) is a global provider of transportation, e-commerce, and business services operating through its Federal Express and FedEx Freight segments. The company offers a wide range of shipping, logistics, printing, and digital solutions to support businesses and consumers worldwide.

Companies valued at $10 billion or more are generally considered "large-cap" stocks, and FedEx fits this criterion. FedEx has grown into a leading player in express delivery and supply chain management.

Shares of the Memphis, Tennessee-based company have declined 9.4% from its 52-week high of $302.02. FDX stock has soared 18.5% over the past three months, outperforming the Nasdaq Composite’s ($NASX) 7.7% gain over the same time frame.

In the longer term, FDX stock is down 2.7% on a YTD basis, lagging behind NASX’s 21% gain. Moreover, shares of the company have decreased 9.6% over the past 52 weeks, compared to NASX’s 22.6% return over the same time frame.

Despite a few fluctuations, the stock has been trading above its 50-day moving average since June.

Shares of FDX rose 2.3% following its Q1 2026 results on Sep. 18 because the company posted solid year-over-year earnings growth, with adjusted operating income increasing to $1.30 billion and adjusted EPS rising to $3.83, driven by strong U.S. domestic package revenue and structural cost reductions. Investors were also encouraged by FedEx’s fiscal 2026 outlook, including 4% - 6% revenue growth and $17.20 - $19 adjusted EPS after excluding optimization, spin-off, and fiscal-year-change costs.

Additionally, confidence improved due to FedEx completing $500 million in share repurchases during the quarter and advancing toward the planned June 2026 spin-off of FedEx Freight.

In contrast, rival United Parcel Service, Inc. (UPS) has lagged behind FDX stock. Shares of United Parcel Service have dipped 24.3% on a YTD basis and 29.6% over the past 52 weeks.

Despite the stock’s underperformance over the past year, analysts remain moderately optimistic on FedEx. The stock has a consensus rating of “Moderate Buy” from 30 analysts in coverage, and as of writing, it is trading above the mean price target of $268.52.

Cailley LaPara and Matthew Griffin

(Bloomberg) -- FedEx Corp. expects profit this quarter to improve from a year ago, easing investor concerns about a lackluster holiday season and volatile trade policies.

Adjusted earnings in its fiscal second quarter, which concludes at the end of November, will surpass the $4.05 a share the courier generated last year, Chief Financial Officer John Dietrich told investors Tuesday at an industry conference. Analysts are anticipating $4.02 a share on average in estimates compiled by Bloomberg.

The comments sent FedEx shares up 5.3% as of 1:38 p.m. in New York. Rival United Parcel Service Inc. climbed as well.

“What you’re seeing right now clearly is something of a relief rally when people have been pretty negative on the prospects for both FedEx and UPS,” said Ari Rosa, an analyst at Citigroup Inc. “That reflects a lot of challenges that these companies have faced over the last 12 to 24 months.”

The package-delivery industry has been grappling with uncertain demand ahead of the peak-shipping season and rising costs from President Donald Trump’s tariffs. FedEx and UPS are also expected to encounter disruptions and higher expenses from the grounding of their MD-11 aircraft following the fatal crash last week of a UPS freighter.

The grounding could be more of a burden for UPS, with the plane type accounting for about 9% of its total fleet, according to filings. The MD-11 represents about 4% of FedEx’s fleet.

The latest developments are pushing the couriers to turn to third-party charters to maintain operations, writes Brian Ossenbeck, an analyst at JP Morgan Securities. The outsourcing is likely to lead to higher costs for the companies, especially as increased demand could push up air freight rates.

“Protecting service during peak comes at a cost,” Ossenbeck wrote in a note.

Simply Wall St

Analysts have nudged their consensus price target for FedEx upward, now forecasting $271.93 from the previous $267.71. This modest increase reflects a growing optimism around FedEx’s near-term potential, supported by fresh operational improvements and encouraging earnings results. Stay tuned to discover how you can track ongoing shifts in sentiment and keep pace with the evolving story around FedEx stock.

[Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value FedEx.](https://www.simplywall.st/company/id/e8cdcdb9-2f1c-48bf-aa39-92af2e595877/valuation?utm_medium=finance_user&utm_campaign=cta_valuation_alternatives&utm_source=yahoo)

## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

Do your thoughts align with the Bull or Bear Analysts? Perhaps you think there's more to the story. ## What's in the News

* FedEx is securing additional freighters after indefinitely grounding its MD-11 jet fleet. This move is intended to help manage operational complexities during the busy holiday shipping season, as reported by Bloomberg.
* At its recent Analyst and Investor Day, FedEx presented ongoing initiatives that prioritize operational improvements and maintain strict cost discipline.
* The company has updated its guidance for fiscal year 2026 and now expects revenue growth between 4 percent and 6 percent, depending on how both domestic and international markets perform.
* FedEx completed a significant share buyback, repurchasing over 2.1 million shares for nearly $500 million. This was part of a broader $3.5 billion repurchase program.

## How This Changes the Fair Value For FedEx

* The consensus analyst price target has risen slightly from $267.71 to $271.93. This reflects greater optimism around FedEx's near-term valuation.
* The discount rate increased modestly from 8.76% to 8.89%. This suggests a marginal rise in perceived risk or required returns.
* Revenue growth estimates show a negligible uptick, moving from 4.01% to 4.01% on a projected annual basis.
* Net profit margin remains virtually unchanged, easing marginally from 5.32% to 5.32%.
* The future P/E ratio edged higher from 14.36x to 14.64x. This indicates slightly elevated expectations for future earnings multiples.

# FedEx Corp. Board Declares Quarterly Dividend

**MEMPHIS, Tenn., November 21, 2025**--([BUSINESS WIRE](https://www.businesswire.com))--The Board of Directors of FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) today declared a quarterly cash dividend of $1.45 per share on FedEx Corp. common stock, in line with the company’s continued focus on delivering stockholder value. The dividend is payable January 6, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 15, 2025.

FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce and business services. With annual revenue of $89 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. Consistently ranked among the world’s most admired and trusted employers, FedEx inspires its more than 500,000 employees to remain focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards and the needs of their customers and communities. FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040. # Is FedEx Stock Underperforming the Nasdaq?

Sohini Mondal

2 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.85%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

[^IXIC

-0.38%](/quote/%5EIXIC/ "^IXIC")

With a market cap of $65 billion, FedEx Corporation (FDX) is a global provider of transportation, e-commerce, and business services operating through its Federal Express and FedEx Freight segments. The company offers a wide range of shipping, logistics, printing, and digital solutions to support businesses and consumers worldwide.

Companies valued at $10 billion or more are generally considered "large-cap" stocks, and FedEx fits this criterion. FedEx has grown into a leading player in express delivery and supply chain management.

Shares of the Memphis, Tennessee-based company have declined 9.4% from its 52-week high of $302.02. FDX stock has soared 18.5% over the past three months, outperforming the Nasdaq Composite’s ($NASX) 7.7% gain over the same time frame.

In the longer term, FDX stock is down 2.7% on a YTD basis, lagging behind NASX’s 21% gain. Moreover, shares of the company have decreased 9.6% over the past 52 weeks, compared to NASX’s 22.6% return over the same time frame.

Despite a few fluctuations, the stock has been trading above its 50-day moving average since June.

Shares of FDX rose 2.3% following its Q1 2026 results on Sep. 18 because the company posted solid year-over-year earnings growth, with adjusted operating income increasing to $1.30 billion and adjusted EPS rising to $3.83, driven by strong U.S. domestic package revenue and structural cost reductions. Investors were also encouraged by FedEx’s fiscal 2026 outlook, including 4% - 6% revenue growth and $17.20 - $19 adjusted EPS after excluding optimization, spin-off, and fiscal-year-change costs.

Additionally, confidence improved due to FedEx completing $500 million in share repurchases during the quarter and advancing toward the planned June 2026 spin-off of FedEx Freight.

In contrast, rival United Parcel Service, Inc. (UPS) has lagged behind FDX stock. Shares of United Parcel Service have dipped 24.3% on a YTD basis and 29.6% over the past 52 weeks.

Despite the stock’s underperformance over the past year, analysts remain moderately optimistic on FedEx. The stock has a consensus rating of “Moderate Buy” from 30 analysts in coverage, and as of writing, it is trading above the mean price target of $268.52.

Cailley LaPara and Matthew Griffin

(Bloomberg) -- FedEx Corp. expects profit this quarter to improve from a year ago, easing investor concerns about a lackluster holiday season and volatile trade policies.

Adjusted earnings in its fiscal second quarter, which concludes at the end of November, will surpass the $4.05 a share the courier generated last year, Chief Financial Officer John Dietrich told investors Tuesday at an industry conference. Analysts are anticipating $4.02 a share on average in estimates compiled by Bloomberg.

The comments sent FedEx shares up 5.3% as of 1:38 p.m. in New York. Rival United Parcel Service Inc. climbed as well.

“What you’re seeing right now clearly is something of a relief rally when people have been pretty negative on the prospects for both FedEx and UPS,” said Ari Rosa, an analyst at Citigroup Inc. “That reflects a lot of challenges that these companies have faced over the last 12 to 24 months.”

The package-delivery industry has been grappling with uncertain demand ahead of the peak-shipping season and rising costs from President Donald Trump’s tariffs. FedEx and UPS are also expected to encounter disruptions and higher expenses from the grounding of their MD-11 aircraft following the fatal crash last week of a UPS freighter.

The grounding could be more of a burden for UPS, with the plane type accounting for about 9% of its total fleet, according to filings. The MD-11 represents about 4% of FedEx’s fleet.

The latest developments are pushing the couriers to turn to third-party charters to maintain operations, writes Brian Ossenbeck, an analyst at JP Morgan Securities. The outsourcing is likely to lead to higher costs for the companies, especially as increased demand could push up air freight rates.

“Protecting service during peak comes at a cost,” Ossenbeck wrote in a note.

This modest increase reflects a growing optimism around FedEx’s near-term potential, supported by fresh operational improvements and encouraging earnings results. ## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

## What's in the News

* FedEx is securing additional freighters after indefinitely grounding its MD-11 jet fleet. This move is intended to help manage operational complexities during the busy holiday shipping season, as reported by Bloomberg.
* At its recent Analyst and Investor Day, FedEx presented ongoing initiatives that prioritize operational improvements and maintain strict cost discipline.
* The company has updated its guidance for fiscal year 2026 and now expects revenue growth between 4 percent and 6 percent, depending on how both domestic and international markets perform.
* FedEx completed a significant share buyback, repurchasing over 2.1 million shares for nearly $500 million. This was part of a broader $3.5 billion repurchase program.

## How This Changes the Fair Value For FedEx

* The consensus analyst price target has risen slightly from $267.71 to $271.93. This reflects greater optimism around FedEx's near-term valuation.
* The discount rate increased modestly from 8.76% to 8.89%. This suggests a marginal rise in perceived risk or required returns.
* Revenue growth estimates show a negligible uptick, moving from 4.01% to 4.01% on a projected annual basis.
* Net profit margin remains virtually unchanged, easing marginally from 5.32% to 5.32%.
* The future P/E ratio edged higher from 14.36x to 14.64x. This indicates slightly elevated expectations for future earnings multiples.

# FedEx Corp. Board Declares Quarterly Dividend

Business Wire

1 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

+1.33%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

**MEMPHIS, Tenn., November 21, 2025**--([BUSINESS WIRE](https://www.businesswire.com))--The Board of Directors of FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) today declared a quarterly cash dividend of $1.45 per share on FedEx Corp. common stock, in line with the company’s continued focus on delivering stockholder value. The dividend is payable January 6, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 15, 2025.

FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce and business services. With annual revenue of $89 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. Consistently ranked among the world’s most admired and trusted employers, FedEx inspires its more than 500,000 employees to remain focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards and the needs of their customers and communities. FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040. # Is FedEx Stock Underperforming the Nasdaq?

Sohini Mondal

2 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.85%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

[^IXIC

-0.38%](/quote/%5EIXIC/ "^IXIC")

With a market cap of $65 billion, FedEx Corporation (FDX) is a global provider of transportation, e-commerce, and business services operating through its Federal Express and FedEx Freight segments. The company offers a wide range of shipping, logistics, printing, and digital solutions to support businesses and consumers worldwide.

Companies valued at $10 billion or more are generally considered "large-cap" stocks, and FedEx fits this criterion. FedEx has grown into a leading player in express delivery and supply chain management.

Shares of the Memphis, Tennessee-based company have declined 9.4% from its 52-week high of $302.02. FDX stock has soared 18.5% over the past three months, outperforming the Nasdaq Composite’s ($NASX) 7.7% gain over the same time frame.

In the longer term, FDX stock is down 2.7% on a YTD basis, lagging behind NASX’s 21% gain. Moreover, shares of the company have decreased 9.6% over the past 52 weeks, compared to NASX’s 22.6% return over the same time frame.

Despite a few fluctuations, the stock has been trading above its 50-day moving average since June.

Shares of FDX rose 2.3% following its Q1 2026 results on Sep. 18 because the company posted solid year-over-year earnings growth, with adjusted operating income increasing to $1.30 billion and adjusted EPS rising to $3.83, driven by strong U.S. domestic package revenue and structural cost reductions. Investors were also encouraged by FedEx’s fiscal 2026 outlook, including 4% - 6% revenue growth and $17.20 - $19 adjusted EPS after excluding optimization, spin-off, and fiscal-year-change costs.

Additionally, confidence improved due to FedEx completing $500 million in share repurchases during the quarter and advancing toward the planned June 2026 spin-off of FedEx Freight.

In contrast, rival United Parcel Service, Inc. (UPS) has lagged behind FDX stock. Shares of United Parcel Service have dipped 24.3% on a YTD basis and 29.6% over the past 52 weeks.

Despite the stock’s underperformance over the past year, analysts remain moderately optimistic on FedEx. The stock has a consensus rating of “Moderate Buy” from 30 analysts in coverage, and as of writing, it is trading above the mean price target of $268.52.

Cailley LaPara and Matthew Griffin

2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- FedEx Corp. expects profit this quarter to improve from a year ago, easing investor concerns about a lackluster holiday season and volatile trade policies.

Adjusted earnings in its fiscal second quarter, which concludes at the end of November, will surpass the $4.05 a share the courier generated last year, Chief Financial Officer John Dietrich told investors Tuesday at an industry conference. Analysts are anticipating $4.02 a share on average in estimates compiled by Bloomberg.

The comments sent FedEx shares up 5.3% as of 1:38 p.m. in New York. Rival United Parcel Service Inc. climbed as well.

“What you’re seeing right now clearly is something of a relief rally when people have been pretty negative on the prospects for both FedEx and UPS,” said Ari Rosa, an analyst at Citigroup Inc. “That reflects a lot of challenges that these companies have faced over the last 12 to 24 months.”

The package-delivery industry has been grappling with uncertain demand ahead of the peak-shipping season and rising costs from President Donald Trump’s tariffs. FedEx and UPS are also expected to encounter disruptions and higher expenses from the grounding of their MD-11 aircraft following the fatal crash last week of a UPS freighter.

The grounding could be more of a burden for UPS, with the plane type accounting for about 9% of its total fleet, according to filings. The MD-11 represents about 4% of FedEx’s fleet.

The latest developments are pushing the couriers to turn to third-party charters to maintain operations, writes Brian Ossenbeck, an analyst at JP Morgan Securities. The outsourcing is likely to lead to higher costs for the companies, especially as increased demand could push up air freight rates.

“Protecting service during peak comes at a cost,” Ossenbeck wrote in a note.

This modest increase reflects a growing optimism around FedEx’s near-term potential, supported by fresh operational improvements and encouraging earnings results. ## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

## What's in the News

* FedEx is securing additional freighters after indefinitely grounding its MD-11 jet fleet. This move is intended to help manage operational complexities during the busy holiday shipping season, as reported by Bloomberg.
* At its recent Analyst and Investor Day, FedEx presented ongoing initiatives that prioritize operational improvements and maintain strict cost discipline.
* The company has updated its guidance for fiscal year 2026 and now expects revenue growth between 4 percent and 6 percent, depending on how both domestic and international markets perform.
* FedEx completed a significant share buyback, repurchasing over 2.1 million shares for nearly $500 million. This was part of a broader $3.5 billion repurchase program.

## How This Changes the Fair Value For FedEx

* The consensus analyst price target has risen slightly from $267.71 to $271.93. This reflects greater optimism around FedEx's near-term valuation.
* The discount rate increased modestly from 8.76% to 8.89%. This suggests a marginal rise in perceived risk or required returns.
* Revenue growth estimates show a negligible uptick, moving from 4.01% to 4.01% on a projected annual basis.
* Net profit margin remains virtually unchanged, easing marginally from 5.32% to 5.32%.
* The future P/E ratio edged higher from 14.36x to 14.64x. This indicates slightly elevated expectations for future earnings multiples.

# FedEx Corp. Board Declares Quarterly Dividend

Business Wire

1 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

+1.33%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

**MEMPHIS, Tenn., November 21, 2025**--([BUSINESS WIRE](https://www.businesswire.com))--The Board of Directors of FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) today declared a quarterly cash dividend of $1.45 per share on FedEx Corp. common stock, in line with the company’s continued focus on delivering stockholder value. The dividend is payable January 6, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 15, 2025.

FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce and business services. With annual revenue of $89 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. Consistently ranked among the world’s most admired and trusted employers, FedEx inspires its more than 500,000 employees to remain focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards and the needs of their customers and communities. FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040. 2 min read

With a market cap of $65 billion, FedEx Corporation (FDX) is a global provider of transportation, e-commerce, and business services operating through its Federal Express and FedEx Freight segments. The company offers a wide range of shipping, logistics, printing, and digital solutions to support businesses and consumers worldwide.

Companies valued at $10 billion or more are generally considered "large-cap" stocks, and FedEx fits this criterion. FedEx has grown into a leading player in express delivery and supply chain management.

Shares of the Memphis, Tennessee-based company have declined 9.4% from its 52-week high of $302.02. FDX stock has soared 18.5% over the past three months, outperforming the Nasdaq Composite’s ($NASX) 7.7% gain over the same time frame.

In the longer term, FDX stock is down 2.7% on a YTD basis, lagging behind NASX’s 21% gain. Moreover, shares of the company have decreased 9.6% over the past 52 weeks, compared to NASX’s 22.6% return over the same time frame.

Despite a few fluctuations, the stock has been trading above its 50-day moving average since June.

Shares of FDX rose 2.3% following its Q1 2026 results on Sep. 18 because the company posted solid year-over-year earnings growth, with adjusted operating income increasing to $1.30 billion and adjusted EPS rising to $3.83, driven by strong U.S. domestic package revenue and structural cost reductions. Investors were also encouraged by FedEx’s fiscal 2026 outlook, including 4% - 6% revenue growth and $17.20 - $19 adjusted EPS after excluding optimization, spin-off, and fiscal-year-change costs.

Additionally, confidence improved due to FedEx completing $500 million in share repurchases during the quarter and advancing toward the planned June 2026 spin-off of FedEx Freight.

In contrast, rival United Parcel Service, Inc. (UPS) has lagged behind FDX stock. Shares of United Parcel Service have dipped 24.3% on a YTD basis and 29.6% over the past 52 weeks.

Despite the stock’s underperformance over the past year, analysts remain moderately optimistic on FedEx. The stock has a consensus rating of “Moderate Buy” from 30 analysts in coverage, and as of writing, it is trading above the mean price target of $268.52.

# FedEx Climbs as Profit Guidance Eases Holiday Season Worries

Cailley LaPara and Matthew Griffin

2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- FedEx Corp. expects profit this quarter to improve from a year ago, easing investor concerns about a lackluster holiday season and volatile trade policies.

Adjusted earnings in its fiscal second quarter, which concludes at the end of November, will surpass the $4.05 a share the courier generated last year, Chief Financial Officer John Dietrich told investors Tuesday at an industry conference. Analysts are anticipating $4.02 a share on average in estimates compiled by Bloomberg.

The comments sent FedEx shares up 5.3% as of 1:38 p.m. in New York. Rival United Parcel Service Inc. climbed as well.

“What you’re seeing right now clearly is something of a relief rally when people have been pretty negative on the prospects for both FedEx and UPS,” said Ari Rosa, an analyst at Citigroup Inc. “That reflects a lot of challenges that these companies have faced over the last 12 to 24 months.”

The package-delivery industry has been grappling with uncertain demand ahead of the peak-shipping season and rising costs from President Donald Trump’s tariffs. FedEx and UPS are also expected to encounter disruptions and higher expenses from the grounding of their MD-11 aircraft following the fatal crash last week of a UPS freighter.

The grounding could be more of a burden for UPS, with the plane type accounting for about 9% of its total fleet, according to filings. The MD-11 represents about 4% of FedEx’s fleet.

The latest developments are pushing the couriers to turn to third-party charters to maintain operations, writes Brian Ossenbeck, an analyst at JP Morgan Securities. The outsourcing is likely to lead to higher costs for the companies, especially as increased demand could push up air freight rates.

“Protecting service during peak comes at a cost,” Ossenbeck wrote in a note.

Analysts have nudged their consensus price target for FedEx upward, now forecasting $271.93 from the previous $267.71. This modest increase reflects a growing optimism around FedEx’s near-term potential, supported by fresh operational improvements and encouraging earnings results. ## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

## What's in the News

* FedEx is securing additional freighters after indefinitely grounding its MD-11 jet fleet. This move is intended to help manage operational complexities during the busy holiday shipping season, as reported by Bloomberg.
* At its recent Analyst and Investor Day, FedEx presented ongoing initiatives that prioritize operational improvements and maintain strict cost discipline.
* The company has updated its guidance for fiscal year 2026 and now expects revenue growth between 4 percent and 6 percent, depending on how both domestic and international markets perform.
* FedEx completed a significant share buyback, repurchasing over 2.1 million shares for nearly $500 million. This was part of a broader $3.5 billion repurchase program.

## How This Changes the Fair Value For FedEx

* The consensus analyst price target has risen slightly from $267.71 to $271.93. This reflects greater optimism around FedEx's near-term valuation.
* The discount rate increased modestly from 8.76% to 8.89%. This suggests a marginal rise in perceived risk or required returns.
* Revenue growth estimates show a negligible uptick, moving from 4.01% to 4.01% on a projected annual basis.
* Net profit margin remains virtually unchanged, easing marginally from 5.32% to 5.32%.
* The future P/E ratio edged higher from 14.36x to 14.64x. This indicates slightly elevated expectations for future earnings multiples.

# Why FedEx (FDX) is Poised to Beat Earnings Estimates Again

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.85%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

Have you been searching for a stock that might be well-positioned to maintain its earnings-beat streak in its upcoming report? It is worth considering FedEx (FDX), which belongs to the Zacks Transportation - Air Freight and Cargo industry.

This package delivery company has seen a nice streak of beating earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The average surprise for the last two quarters was 3.65%.

For the last reported quarter, FedEx came out with earnings of $3.83 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.65 per share, representing a surprise of 4.93%. For the previous quarter, the company was expected to post earnings of $5.93 per share and it actually produced earnings of $6.07 per share, delivering a surprise of 2.36%.

## Price and EPS Surprise

With this earnings history in mind, recent estimates have been moving higher for FedEx. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the company is positive, which is a great sign of an earnings beat, especially when you combine this metric with its nice Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

FedEx has an Earnings ESP of +1.19% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on December 18, 2025.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

# What Catalysts Are Reshaping the FedEx Story for Investors?

Simply Wall St

5 min read

Analysts have nudged their consensus price target for FedEx upward, now forecasting $271.93 from the previous $267.71. This modest increase reflects a growing optimism around FedEx’s near-term potential, supported by fresh operational improvements and encouraging earnings results. Stay tuned to discover how you can track ongoing shifts in sentiment and keep pace with the evolving story around FedEx stock.

[Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value FedEx.](https://www.simplywall.st/company/id/e8cdcdb9-2f1c-48bf-aa39-92af2e595877/valuation?utm_medium=finance_user&utm_campaign=cta_valuation_alternatives&utm_source=yahoo)

## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

Do your thoughts align with the Bull or Bear Analysts? Perhaps you think there's more to the story. ## What's in the News

* FedEx is securing additional freighters after indefinitely grounding its MD-11 jet fleet. This move is intended to help manage operational complexities during the busy holiday shipping season, as reported by Bloomberg.
* At its recent Analyst and Investor Day, FedEx presented ongoing initiatives that prioritize operational improvements and maintain strict cost discipline.
* The company has updated its guidance for fiscal year 2026 and now expects revenue growth between 4 percent and 6 percent, depending on how both domestic and international markets perform.
* FedEx completed a significant share buyback, repurchasing over 2.1 million shares for nearly $500 million. This was part of a broader $3.5 billion repurchase program.

## How This Changes the Fair Value For FedEx

* The consensus analyst price target has risen slightly from $267.71 to $271.93. This reflects greater optimism around FedEx's near-term valuation.
* The discount rate increased modestly from 8.76% to 8.89%. This suggests a marginal rise in perceived risk or required returns.
* Revenue growth estimates show a negligible uptick, moving from 4.01% to 4.01% on a projected annual basis.
* Net profit margin remains virtually unchanged, easing marginally from 5.32% to 5.32%.
* The future P/E ratio edged higher from 14.36x to 14.64x. This indicates slightly elevated expectations for future earnings multiples.

# Why FedEx (FDX) is Poised to Beat Earnings Estimates Again

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.85%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

Have you been searching for a stock that might be well-positioned to maintain its earnings-beat streak in its upcoming report? It is worth considering FedEx (FDX), which belongs to the Zacks Transportation - Air Freight and Cargo industry.

This package delivery company has seen a nice streak of beating earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The average surprise for the last two quarters was 3.65%.

For the last reported quarter, FedEx came out with earnings of $3.83 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.65 per share, representing a surprise of 4.93%. For the previous quarter, the company was expected to post earnings of $5.93 per share and it actually produced earnings of $6.07 per share, delivering a surprise of 2.36%.

## Price and EPS Surprise

With this earnings history in mind, recent estimates have been moving higher for FedEx. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the company is positive, which is a great sign of an earnings beat, especially when you combine this metric with its nice Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

FedEx has an Earnings ESP of +1.19% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on December 18, 2025.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Because of this, it's really important to check a company's Earnings ESP ahead of its quarterly release to increase the odds of success. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

# What Catalysts Are Reshaping the FedEx Story for Investors?

Simply Wall St

5 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

+0.56%](/quote/TFC/ "TFC")

Analysts have nudged their consensus price target for FedEx upward, now forecasting $271.93 from the previous $267.71. This modest increase reflects a growing optimism around FedEx’s near-term potential, supported by fresh operational improvements and encouraging earnings results. Stay tuned to discover how you can track ongoing shifts in sentiment and keep pace with the evolving story around FedEx stock.

[Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value FedEx.](https://www.simplywall.st/company/id/e8cdcdb9-2f1c-48bf-aa39-92af2e595877/valuation?utm_medium=finance_user&utm_campaign=cta_valuation_alternatives&utm_source=yahoo)

## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

Do your thoughts align with the Bull or Bear Analysts? Perhaps you think there's more to the story. ## What's in the News

* FedEx is securing additional freighters after indefinitely grounding its MD-11 jet fleet. This move is intended to help manage operational complexities during the busy holiday shipping season, as reported by Bloomberg.
* At its recent Analyst and Investor Day, FedEx presented ongoing initiatives that prioritize operational improvements and maintain strict cost discipline.
* The company has updated its guidance for fiscal year 2026 and now expects revenue growth between 4 percent and 6 percent, depending on how both domestic and international markets perform.
* FedEx completed a significant share buyback, repurchasing over 2.1 million shares for nearly $500 million. This was part of a broader $3.5 billion repurchase program.

## How This Changes the Fair Value For FedEx

* The consensus analyst price target has risen slightly from $267.71 to $271.93. This reflects greater optimism around FedEx's near-term valuation.
* The discount rate increased modestly from 8.76% to 8.89%. This suggests a marginal rise in perceived risk or required returns.
* Revenue growth estimates show a negligible uptick, moving from 4.01% to 4.01% on a projected annual basis.
* Net profit margin remains virtually unchanged, easing marginally from 5.32% to 5.32%.
* The future P/E ratio edged higher from 14.36x to 14.64x. This indicates slightly elevated expectations for future earnings multiples.

# Why FedEx (FDX) is Poised to Beat Earnings Estimates Again

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.85%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

Have you been searching for a stock that might be well-positioned to maintain its earnings-beat streak in its upcoming report? It is worth considering FedEx (FDX), which belongs to the Zacks Transportation - Air Freight and Cargo industry.

This package delivery company has seen a nice streak of beating earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The average surprise for the last two quarters was 3.65%.

For the last reported quarter, FedEx came out with earnings of $3.83 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.65 per share, representing a surprise of 4.93%. For the previous quarter, the company was expected to post earnings of $5.93 per share and it actually produced earnings of $6.07 per share, delivering a surprise of 2.36%.

## Price and EPS Surprise

With this earnings history in mind, recent estimates have been moving higher for FedEx. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the company is positive, which is a great sign of an earnings beat, especially when you combine this metric with its nice Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

FedEx has an Earnings ESP of +1.19% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on December 18, 2025.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Analysts have nudged their consensus price target for FedEx upward, now forecasting $271.93 from the previous $267.71. This modest increase reflects a growing optimism around FedEx’s near-term potential, supported by fresh operational improvements and encouraging earnings results. Stay tuned to discover how you can track ongoing shifts in sentiment and keep pace with the evolving story around FedEx stock.

## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

## What's in the News

* FedEx is securing additional freighters after indefinitely grounding its MD-11 jet fleet. This move is intended to help manage operational complexities during the busy holiday shipping season, as reported by Bloomberg.
* At its recent Analyst and Investor Day, FedEx presented ongoing initiatives that prioritize operational improvements and maintain strict cost discipline.
* The company has updated its guidance for fiscal year 2026 and now expects revenue growth between 4 percent and 6 percent, depending on how both domestic and international markets perform.
* FedEx completed a significant share buyback, repurchasing over 2.1 million shares for nearly $500 million. This was part of a broader $3.5 billion repurchase program.

## How This Changes the Fair Value For FedEx

* The consensus analyst price target has risen slightly from $267.71 to $271.93. This reflects greater optimism around FedEx's near-term valuation.
* The discount rate increased modestly from 8.76% to 8.89%. This suggests a marginal rise in perceived risk or required returns.
* Revenue growth estimates show a negligible uptick, moving from 4.01% to 4.01% on a projected annual basis.
* Net profit margin remains virtually unchanged, easing marginally from 5.32% to 5.32%.
* The future P/E ratio edged higher from 14.36x to 14.64x. This indicates slightly elevated expectations for future earnings multiples.
