# Why FedEx (FDX) is Poised to Beat Earnings Estimates Again

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.85%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

Have you been searching for a stock that might be well-positioned to maintain its earnings-beat streak in its upcoming report? It is worth considering FedEx (FDX), which belongs to the Zacks Transportation - Air Freight and Cargo industry.

This package delivery company has seen a nice streak of beating earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The average surprise for the last two quarters was 3.65%.

For the last reported quarter, FedEx came out with earnings of $3.83 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.65 per share, representing a surprise of 4.93%. For the previous quarter, the company was expected to post earnings of $5.93 per share and it actually produced earnings of $6.07 per share, delivering a surprise of 2.36%.

## Price and EPS Surprise

With this earnings history in mind, recent estimates have been moving higher for FedEx. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the company is positive, which is a great sign of an earnings beat, especially when you combine this metric with its nice Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

FedEx has an Earnings ESP of +1.19% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on December 18, 2025.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Have you been searching for a stock that might be well-positioned to maintain its earnings-beat streak in its upcoming report? It is worth considering FedEx (FDX), which belongs to the Zacks Transportation - Air Freight and Cargo industry.

This package delivery company has seen a nice streak of beating earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The average surprise for the last two quarters was 3.65%.

For the last reported quarter, FedEx came out with earnings of $3.83 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.65 per share, representing a surprise of 4.93%. For the previous quarter, the company was expected to post earnings of $5.93 per share and it actually produced earnings of $6.07 per share, delivering a surprise of 2.36%.

## Price and EPS Surprise

With this earnings history in mind, recent estimates have been moving higher for FedEx. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the company is positive, which is a great sign of an earnings beat, especially when you combine this metric with its nice Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

FedEx has an Earnings ESP of +1.19% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on December 18, 2025.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Analysts have nudged their consensus price target for FedEx upward, now forecasting $271.93 from the previous $267.71. This modest increase reflects a growing optimism around FedEx’s near-term potential, supported by fresh operational improvements and encouraging earnings results. Stay tuned to discover how you can track ongoing shifts in sentiment and keep pace with the evolving story around FedEx stock.

## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

## What's in the News

* FedEx is securing additional freighters after indefinitely grounding its MD-11 jet fleet. This move is intended to help manage operational complexities during the busy holiday shipping season, as reported by Bloomberg.
* At its recent Analyst and Investor Day, FedEx presented ongoing initiatives that prioritize operational improvements and maintain strict cost discipline.
* The company has updated its guidance for fiscal year 2026 and now expects revenue growth between 4 percent and 6 percent, depending on how both domestic and international markets perform.
* FedEx completed a significant share buyback, repurchasing over 2.1 million shares for nearly $500 million. This was part of a broader $3.5 billion repurchase program.

## How This Changes the Fair Value For FedEx

* The consensus analyst price target has risen slightly from $267.71 to $271.93. This reflects greater optimism around FedEx's near-term valuation.
* The discount rate increased modestly from 8.76% to 8.89%. This suggests a marginal rise in perceived risk or required returns.
* Revenue growth estimates show a negligible uptick, moving from 4.01% to 4.01% on a projected annual basis.
* Net profit margin remains virtually unchanged, easing marginally from 5.32% to 5.32%.
* The future P/E ratio edged higher from 14.36x to 14.64x. This indicates slightly elevated expectations for future earnings multiples.

# Why FedEx (FDX) is Poised to Beat Earnings Estimates Again

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[FDX

-0.85%](/quote/FDX/ "FDX")

Have you been searching for a stock that might be well-positioned to maintain its earnings-beat streak in its upcoming report? It is worth considering FedEx (FDX), which belongs to the Zacks Transportation - Air Freight and Cargo industry.

This package delivery company has seen a nice streak of beating earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The average surprise for the last two quarters was 3.65%.

For the last reported quarter, FedEx came out with earnings of $3.83 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.65 per share, representing a surprise of 4.93%. For the previous quarter, the company was expected to post earnings of $5.93 per share and it actually produced earnings of $6.07 per share, delivering a surprise of 2.36%.

## Price and EPS Surprise

With this earnings history in mind, recent estimates have been moving higher for FedEx. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the company is positive, which is a great sign of an earnings beat, especially when you combine this metric with its nice Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

FedEx has an Earnings ESP of +1.19% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on December 18, 2025.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

## What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Recent research from Wall Street analysts reflects a mix of optimism and caution regarding FedEx’s performance and outlook. Here are the key takeaways from their commentary:

**🐂 Bullish Takeaways**

* **Citi** raised its price target for FedEx to $310 from $279 and reiterated a Buy rating after meeting with management. Citi highlighted that FedEx’s cost cutting momentum is building and sees potential for upside if the macroeconomic environment improves.
* **Truist** increased its price target to $285 from $275, maintaining a Buy rating. The firm notes a stabilizing freight market, improving cost discipline, and management’s constructive but cautious tone heading into Q3 results.
* **UBS** lifted its price target to $314 from $293, emphasizing stronger year-over-year revenue growth and margin improvement in the most recent quarter. UBS commented that FedEx’s results prompted a positive market response, especially given earlier negative sentiment.
* **TD Cowen** raised its price target to $271 from $269, commending FedEx for beating expectations in fiscal Q1 despite trade policy challenges. They note steady top line growth expectations.
* **Stifel** kept a Buy rating, adjusting its target slightly lower to $296 from $308, and recognized the strong Q1 adjusted EPS as evidence of execution on FedEx’s transformation initiatives.
* Multiple firms, including **Bernstein** and **Wells Fargo**, have also upped targets, citing earnings outperformance and improved execution despite mixed external conditions.
* Key drivers rewarded by analysts include ongoing cost discipline, margin improvements, effective execution, and early signs of growth momentum.
* Some firms remain attentive to management’s guidance and transparency, pointing to improved communication as a positive.

**🐻 Bearish Takeaways**

* **JPMorgan** downgraded FedEx to Neutral from Overweight and reduced its price target to $274 from $284. The firm cited concerns about the company’s full year earnings guidance, specifically the risk that forecasts depend on a rebound in freight fundamentals that may not materialize.
* **Raymond James** lowered its target to $255 from $260, highlighting persistent challenges related to tariffs and their impact on both pricing and consumer demand as the holiday season approaches.
* **UBS** also previously cut their target to $293 from $297 due to weaker-than-expected volume trends and underperformance in the less-than-truckload segment, warning that earnings forecasts have been trimmed heading into recent reports.
* Bearish and neutral analysts are focused on lingering external risks such as tariffs, trade headwinds, and the dependency on a meaningful demand recovery for a sustained rebound.
* Reservations remain regarding the valuation, with some caution that potential upside is already reflected in current prices, and near-term risks tied to operating leverage and the possibility of underwhelming earnings realization.

## FedEx Corporation Overview Integrated Freight & Logistics / Industrials

FedEx Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, provides transportation, e-commerce, and business services in the United States and internationally. It operates through Federal Express and FedEx Freight segments. The company offers transportation services, including express, freight, less-than-truckload freight, and time-specific freight-shipping; and small-package ground delivery services. It also provides e-commerce and digital solutions; dataworks; printing and shipping management, including digital printing, professional finishing, document creation, design solutions, direct mail, signs and graphics, custom-branded boxes, copying, computer rental, free Wi-Fi, corporate print solutions, shredding, expedited U.S. passport processing and renewal, and digital notarization; packing services, as well as packing supplies and boxes; document and business services; and retail access for package transportation. In addition, the company offers logistics services, air and ocean freight-forwarding and cargo transportation, specialty transportation, customs brokerage and clearance, trade management tools and data, and door-to-door solutions; and third party logistics and supply chain management solutions, such as inbound logistics, warehousing and distribution, fulfillment, contract packaging and product configuration, systems integration, returns process and disposition, test, repair, refurbishment, and product liquidation. Further, it provides sales, marketing, administrative, information technology, and back-office support services. FedEx Corporation was founded in 1971 and is headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee.

### FedEx's Domestic Package Volumes Show Resilience Heading Into Fiscal 2026

FedEx pioneered overnight delivery in 1973 and remains the world's largest express package provider. In fiscal 2025, the firm's Federal Express segment—which houses the core package delivery operations—made up 86% of total revenue, with 10% coming from FedEx Freight, its asset-based less-than-truckload shipping segment. The remainder came from other services, including FedEx Office, which provides document production/shipping, and FedEx Logistics, which provides global forwarding. FedEx acquired Dutch parcel delivery firm TNT Express in 2016, boosting its presence across Europe. TNT was previously the fourth-largest global parcel delivery provider.

FedEx Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, provides transportation, e-commerce, and business services in the United States and internationally. FedEx has announced a global AI Education and Literacy programme aimed at equipping its workforce with skills to work with new technologies across its operations. The company said the initiative will provide personalised, role-based training for employees in all regions.

FedEx noted that the programme is part of its multi-year transformation plan in which it is adopting AI-powered tools to improve supply chain performance. The training will focus on building common AI fluency and developing capabilities to apply the technology in day-to-day functions.

“The future of business is being shaped by data and AI more than ever before,” said Raj Subramaniam, president and CEO, FedEx Corporation. "Our people remain at the heart of everything we do as FedEx continues its evolution into an AI-powered enterprise." We’re investing in AI education tools to help our team members grow their skills, support safer, smarter work, and unlock new opportunities across the business.”

FedEx has partnered with Accenture to design and deliver specialised AI training modules. Accenture will use its LearnVantage platform to create scalable programmes that include skill recognition and live sessions. The company said these modules will give employees personalised pathways to build AI literacy aligned with their roles and career goals.

The training will focus on creating a shared understanding of technology and responsible AI use across the organisation. FedEx said employees will gain the skills to apply AI within their functions, while leaders will receive guidance on integrating AI into team activities and wider processes.

“We are on a journey to empower our people with AI literacy and the practical technology skills needed to keep driving our business forward,” said Vishal Talwar, chief digital and information officer, FedEx Corporation. “As we create a shared, common understanding of AI internally at FedEx, team members will have access to modules, AI certifications, and mastery opportunities to help them grow in their careers.”

“FedEx is making supply chains smarter for everyone by putting its people at the centre and providing them with the training they need to thrive in the age of AI,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “We are excited to partner with FedEx to deliver role-based training that enables its employees to use AI responsibly, discover new ways of working, and confidently drive transformational change.”

MEMPHIS, Tenn. Dec. 2, 2025 – FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) today announced the launch of an enterprise-wide AI Education and Literacy program, which includes personalized, roles-based trainings for team members around the world. This program reinforces the company’s commitment to investing in the development of its people, consistent with its culture.

As part of a multi-year transformation journey, the company is using AI-powered solutions to make supply chains smarter for everyone. This AI Education and Literacy program will build common AI fluency and skills across the global FedEx enterprise, helping team members develop and enhance capabilities to apply AI responsibly and effectively.

“The future of business is being shaped by data and AI more than ever before,” said Raj Subramaniam, president and CEO, FedEx Corporation. “As FedEx continues its evolution into an AI-powered enterprise, our people remain at the heart of everything we do. We’re investing in AI education tools to help our team members grow their skills; support safer, smarter work; and unlock new opportunities across the business.”

In addition to building out internal training programs that expand on AI fundamentals, FedEx has tapped Accenture to provide customized AI education programs. Through its AI-native training platform LearnVantage, Accenture will provide tailored, scalable training, complete with skill recognition and interactive live training sessions to drive adoption. Personalized skilling pathways will also empower FedEx team members to build AI literacy depending on where they are on their professional growth journey.

The enhanced AI training offering is designed to create a shared language of technology understanding across the FedEx team. Employees will learn the skills they need to apply AI responsibly within their function. FedEx leaders will be equipped with the knowledge of how to embed AI into their own work, their teams’ work, and cross-functional processes to drive transformational change.

“We are on a journey to empower our people with AI literacy and the practical technology skills needed to keep driving our business forward,” said Vishal Talwar, chief digital and information officer, FedEx Corporation. “As we create a shared, common understanding of AI internally at FedEx, team members will have access to modules, AI certifications, and mastery opportunities to help grow in their careers.”

“FedEx is making supply chains smarter for everyone by putting its people at the center and providing them with the training they need to thrive in the age of AI,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “We are excited to partner with FedEx to deliver role-based training that enables its employees to use AI responsibly, discover new ways of working, and confidently drive transformational change. Together, we can help unlock the full value of AI across the company.”

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 30

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week higher as markets cheered signs of slower [inflation](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators/inflation-rate) and rising odds of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.54%, the Nasdaq **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** rose 0.78%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** added 0.61%. Treasury yields eased, with the 10-year note [closing at 4.00%.](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators)

Economic data showed cooling trends in both prices and growth. The inflation rate [stood at 3.01%](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), unemployment edged up to 4.40%, and real GDP growth came in at 3.80%. Retail sales rose a modest 0.07%, signaling that consumers are still spending, but at a slower pace. The Federal Funds Rate was 4.09%, down slightly from September.

In commodities, silver **[(XAGUSD)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:xagusd)** surged 6.49% to $57.09 per ounce, hitting record highs for the year. Gold **[(XAUUSD)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:xauusd)** rose 1.29%, while oil prices [slipped 0.29%](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl) to $58.48 a barrel. Natural gas jumped 6.67%, reflecting colder weather forecasts and strong export demand.

## **Big Tech Takes a Breather**

The story of the week was the pullback in major technology names after a strong year of gains. **Nvidia** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) fell 1.81%, its worst month since 2022, as investors rotated away from high-growth stocks. The decline followed reports that **Meta Platforms** [(META)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/meta) may buy [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) chips from **Alphabet** [(GOOGL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/googl) instead of Nvidia, sparking talk that Nvidia’s market dominance could face its first real test.

Meanwhile, Alphabet climbed 13.8% for the month after revealing its upgraded Gemini 3 AI model and a potential new chip deal with Meta. **Broadcom** [(AVGO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/avgo) also gained 7.6% on expectations it will benefit from demand tied to Google’s AI projects. However, investors grew more selective, with many looking to take profits from names that led the 2025 rally.

The rotation weighed on the broader AI trade, but it also reflected healthy rebalancing. Analysts said investors are adjusting to the idea that AI spending growth may spread to more firms and chip designs. The shift helped steady markets as traders prepared for what some call a “Santa Claus rally” fueled by rate-cut expectations.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

Defense startup **Anduril** grabbed headlines after a *Wall Street Journal* report said its autonomous drone systems failed multiple field tests. The company, founded by Palmer Luckey and backed by Peter Thiel, said the issues were part of its “fail fast” approach to innovation. Still, the news raised fresh questions about the reliability of AI weapons systems in active use.

Another major story centered on **OpenAI’s** financing model. *The Financial Times* reported that partners, including **Oracle** [(ORCL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/orcl), **SoftBank** [(SFTBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sftby), **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv), **[Crusoe](https://www.tipranks.com/private-companies/crusoe)**, and **Blue Owl Capital** [(OBDC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/obdc), are [collectively taking on about $100 billion](https://www.tipranks.com/news/softbank-orcl-crwv-take-on-100b-debt-to-fuel-openais-growth-is-it-worth-the-risk) in debt to fund OpenAI’s massive infrastructure projects. Oracle’s stock fell 1.49% on the news, as investors grew wary of rising costs linked to AI data centers. Analysts noted that OpenAI’s strategy of “leveraging other balance sheets” could put pressure on partners even as the company expands globally.

Meanwhile, **GameStop** [(GME)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gme) made a surprise comeback, rising more than 3% after [Michael Burry](https://www.tipranks.com/experts/hedge-funds/michael-burry) shared old letters and emails from his time investing in the retailer. The nostalgic posts reignited chatter among retail traders, making GameStop one of the most mentioned tickers on social media. Still, analysts said the move had little to do with fundamentals.

**Intel** [(INTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/intc) was the standout among large-cap stocks, gaining over 10% for the week as investors welcomed signs of renewed strength in the chipmaker’s PC business. Other gainers included **Moderna** [(MRNA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mrna), **SanDisk** [(SNDK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sndk), and **Western Digital** [(WDC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wdc), each rising between 3% and 4%.

## **The Week Ahead**

Looking ahead, attention turns to the Federal Reserve’s December policy meeting, where traders now see an 80% chance of a quarter-point rate cut. Investors will also watch for November jobs data and updates from the manufacturing sector for clues on the strength of the economy heading into 2026.

With inflation cooling and borrowing costs easing, analysts expect continued support for equities into year-end. However, as the AI trade resets and market leadership shifts, volatility may stay elevated. For now, the market mood appears steady, with investors cautiously optimistic that the next Fed move could mark the start of a softer monetary path.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The [earnings calendar](https://www.tipranks.com/calendars/earnings) stays active this week, with software, cybersecurity, and retail names taking center stage as the final wave of November results rolls in.

On Tuesday, **Salesforce** [(CRM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crm) will headline after the close, with investors watching for updates on enterprise software demand and margins following steady growth in cloud revenue. **Snowflake** [(SNOW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/snow) will also report, with Wall Street focusing on consumption trends across data analytics workloads. Wednesday brings key reports from **CrowdStrike Holdings** [(CRWD)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwd), **Marvell Technology** [(MRVL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mrvl), and **Okta** [(OKTA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/okta), all offering a closer look at cybersecurity budgets and chip sector demand.

Later in the week, **MongoDB** [(MDB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mdb) and **Credo Technology Group** [(CRDO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crdo) will release earnings after the close. Both companies carry strong buy ratings, with analysts expecting continued growth in cloud database adoption and connectivity hardware demand. **Hewlett Packard Enterprise** [(HPE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpe) and **Ulta Beauty** [(ULTA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ulta) will follow on Thursday, giving the market a read on enterprise software spending, IT infrastructure, and consumer retail resilience.

Rounding out the week, **Toronto Dominion Bank** [(TD)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/td), **Kroger Company** [(KR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/kr), and **Dollar General** [(DG)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dg) will report before the open on Friday.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

A new week brings a broad lineup of dividend-paying companies across industries, from blue-chip tech to consumer goods and financials.

Starting the week, **Coca-Cola** [(KO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ko) and **McDonald’s** [(MCD)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mcd) will pay $0.51 and $1.86 per share. **Lockheed Martin** [(LMT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lmt) and **Northrop Grumman** [(NOC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/noc) will follow, paying shareholders $3.45 and $2.31 per share, as defense stocks continue to attract steady income investors.

In the materials and energy space, **Cameco** [(CCJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ccj) and **Agnico Eagle** [(AEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aem) will distribute $0.17 and $0.40, respectively, while Schlumberger [(SLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/slb) is set to pay $0.28 later in the week.

Among the financials, **Bank of America** [(BAC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bac) will pay $0.28 per share, while **Goldman Sachs Group** [(GS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gs) will follow with a $4.00 payout.

Tech investors will see dividends from **Nvidia** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) and **Qualcomm** (QCOM), which will pay $0.01 and $0.89 per share, respectively.

Consumer and retail names remain active, too. **Nike** [(NKE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nke) will pay $0.41 per share, while **PepsiCo** [(PEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pep) delivers $1.42 and **Union Pacific** [(UNP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/unp) returns $1.38 per share.

Finally, large-cap industrials like **Waste Management** [(WM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wm) and **Dominion Energy** [(D)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/d) will offer $0.82 and $0.67, respectively, while **BlackRock** [(BLK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/blk) will distribute a sizable $5.21 per share.

# Bears RB D'Andre Swift wins FedEx Ground Player of the Week

![Bears Wire](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/lfI5l1HsZMS4KwdDWqASXQ--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTIxNjtoPTU2O2NmPXdlYnA-/https://s.yimg.com/os/creatr-uploaded-images/2020-11/8bd69bd0-2b14-11eb-bfdf-bdeafc7a4bfc)
![Bears Wire](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/6nCYv6pO3XayM6pVSquyZA--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTIxNjtoPTU2O2NmPXdlYnA-/https://s.yimg.com/os/creatr-uploaded-images/2020-11/68102180-2b14-11eb-9bdf-1dc8a9ab45a7)
![](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/wD09M.q58CLOZq16kWxRmA--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTk2MDtoPTY3NztjZj13ZWJw/https://media.zenfs.com/en/chicago_bears_wire_usa_today_sports_articles_533/815bc036872e5696d9397c94c61e6a7e)

The [Chicago Bears](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/chicago-bears/326) ran all over the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/philadelphia-eagles/354) on Black Friday, winning 24-15, and one player is getting recognized for his efforts in the victory.

Running back D'Andre Swift has been named the FedEx Ground Player of the Week after he gashed the Eagles on Friday. Swift carried the ball 18 times for a season-high 125 yards and a touchdown. He was part of an outstanding tandem with rookie Kyle Monangai, who totaled 130 yards on 22 carries and a touchdown. Together, the duo rushed for 255 yards in one of the most dominant rushing performances in franchise history.

Swift, who has 774 rushing yards and five touchdowns in 11 games, is on pace for a career year in 2025 and has played a significant role in the Bears' 9-3 record. Chicago is atop the NFC going into Week 14 and is playing their best ball of the year as they look to make the postseason for the first time since 2020.

This is the first time Swift has won the FedEx Ground Player of the Week award and the first time a Bears player has won since Khalil Herbert in Week 16 of the 2023 season. Quarterback Caleb Williams won the FedEx Air Player of the Week back in Week 3 following his stellar performance against the Dallas Cowboys. The FedEx Air Player of the Week was [Green Bay Packers](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/green-bay-packers/335) quarterback Jordan Love, whom the Bears play this weekend.

# FedEx launches global AI education programme for its workforce

## The training will focus on building common AI fluency and developing capabilities to apply the technology in day-to-day functions.

By[Our Correspondent

FedEx has announced a global AI Education and Literacy programme aimed at equipping its workforce with skills to work with new technologies across its operations. The company said the initiative will provide personalised, role-based training for employees in all regions.

FedEx noted that the programme is part of its multi-year transformation plan in which it is adopting AI-powered tools to improve supply chain performance. The training will focus on building common AI fluency and developing capabilities to apply the technology in day-to-day functions.

“The future of business is being shaped by data and AI more than ever before,” said Raj Subramaniam, president and CEO, FedEx Corporation. "Our people remain at the heart of everything we do as FedEx continues its evolution into an AI-powered enterprise." We’re investing in AI education tools to help our team members grow their skills, support safer, smarter work, and unlock new opportunities across the business.”

FedEx has partnered with Accenture to design and deliver specialised AI training modules. Accenture will use its LearnVantage platform to create scalable programmes that include skill recognition and live sessions. The company said these modules will give employees personalised pathways to build AI literacy aligned with their roles and career goals.

The training will focus on creating a shared understanding of technology and responsible AI use across the organisation. FedEx said employees will gain the skills to apply AI within their functions, while leaders will receive guidance on integrating AI into team activities and wider processes.

“We are on a journey to empower our people with AI literacy and the practical technology skills needed to keep driving our business forward,” said Vishal Talwar, chief digital and information officer, FedEx Corporation. “As we create a shared, common understanding of AI internally at FedEx, team members will have access to modules, AI certifications, and mastery opportunities to help them grow in their careers.”

“FedEx is making supply chains smarter for everyone by putting its people at the centre and providing them with the training they need to thrive in the age of AI,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “We are excited to partner with FedEx to deliver role-based training that enables its employees to use AI responsibly, discover new ways of working, and confidently drive transformational change.”

MEMPHIS, Tenn. Dec. 2, 2025 – FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) today announced the launch of an enterprise-wide AI Education and Literacy program, which includes personalized, roles-based trainings for team members around the world. This program reinforces the company’s commitment to investing in the development of its people, consistent with its culture.

As part of a multi-year transformation journey, the company is using AI-powered solutions to make supply chains smarter for everyone. This AI Education and Literacy program will build common AI fluency and skills across the global FedEx enterprise, helping team members develop and enhance capabilities to apply AI responsibly and effectively.

“The future of business is being shaped by data and AI more than ever before,” said Raj Subramaniam, president and CEO, FedEx Corporation. “As FedEx continues its evolution into an AI-powered enterprise, our people remain at the heart of everything we do. We’re investing in AI education tools to help our team members grow their skills; support safer, smarter work; and unlock new opportunities across the business.”

In addition to building out internal training programs that expand on AI fundamentals, FedEx has tapped Accenture to provide customized AI education programs. Through its AI-native training platform LearnVantage, Accenture will provide tailored, scalable training, complete with skill recognition and interactive live training sessions to drive adoption. Personalized skilling pathways will also empower FedEx team members to build AI literacy depending on where they are on their professional growth journey.

The enhanced AI training offering is designed to create a shared language of technology understanding across the FedEx team. Employees will learn the skills they need to apply AI responsibly within their function. FedEx leaders will be equipped with the knowledge of how to embed AI into their own work, their teams’ work, and cross-functional processes to drive transformational change.

“We are on a journey to empower our people with AI literacy and the practical technology skills needed to keep driving our business forward,” said Vishal Talwar, chief digital and information officer, FedEx Corporation. “As we create a shared, common understanding of AI internally at FedEx, team members will have access to modules, AI certifications, and mastery opportunities to help grow in their careers.”

“FedEx is making supply chains smarter for everyone by putting its people at the center and providing them with the training they need to thrive in the age of AI,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “We are excited to partner with FedEx to deliver role-based training that enables its employees to use AI responsibly, discover new ways of working, and confidently drive transformational change. Together, we can help unlock the full value of AI across the company.”

**About FedEx Corp.**

FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce, and business services. With annual revenue of $89 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. Consistently ranked among the world’s most admired and trusted employers, FedEx inspires its more than 500,000 employees to remain focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards, and the needs of their customers and communities. FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040. # The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 30

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week higher as markets cheered signs of slower [inflation](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators/inflation-rate) and rising odds of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.54%, the Nasdaq **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** rose 0.78%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** added 0.61%. Treasury yields eased, with the 10-year note [closing at 4.00%.](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators)

### TipRanks Black Friday Sale

* [Claim 60% off TipRanks Premium](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-premium/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  for the data-backed insights and research tools you need to invest with confidence.
* [Subscribe to TipRanks' Smart Investor Picks](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-smartinvestor/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  and see our data in action through our high-performing model portfolio -  now also 60% off

Economic data showed cooling trends in both prices and growth. The inflation rate [stood at 3.01%](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), unemployment edged up to 4.40%, and real GDP growth came in at 3.80%. Retail sales rose a modest 0.07%, signaling that consumers are still spending, but at a slower pace. The Federal Funds Rate was 4.09%, down slightly from September.

In commodities, silver **[(XAGUSD)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:xagusd)** surged 6.49% to $57.09 per ounce, hitting record highs for the year. Gold **[(XAUUSD)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:xauusd)** rose 1.29%, while oil prices [slipped 0.29%](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl) to $58.48 a barrel. Natural gas jumped 6.67%, reflecting colder weather forecasts and strong export demand.

## **Big Tech Takes a Breather**

The story of the week was the pullback in major technology names after a strong year of gains. **Nvidia** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) fell 1.81%, its worst month since 2022, as investors rotated away from high-growth stocks. The decline followed reports that **Meta Platforms** [(META)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/meta) may buy [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) chips from **Alphabet** [(GOOGL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/googl) instead of Nvidia, sparking talk that Nvidia’s market dominance could face its first real test.

Meanwhile, Alphabet climbed 13.8% for the month after revealing its upgraded Gemini 3 AI model and a potential new chip deal with Meta. **Broadcom** [(AVGO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/avgo) also gained 7.6% on expectations it will benefit from demand tied to Google’s AI projects. However, investors grew more selective, with many looking to take profits from names that led the 2025 rally.

The rotation weighed on the broader AI trade, but it also reflected healthy rebalancing. Analysts said investors are adjusting to the idea that AI spending growth may spread to more firms and chip designs. The shift helped steady markets as traders prepared for what some call a “Santa Claus rally” fueled by rate-cut expectations.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

Defense startup **Anduril** grabbed headlines after a *Wall Street Journal* report said its autonomous drone systems failed multiple field tests. The company, founded by Palmer Luckey and backed by Peter Thiel, said the issues were part of its “fail fast” approach to innovation. Still, the news raised fresh questions about the reliability of AI weapons systems in active use.

Another major story centered on **OpenAI’s** financing model. *The Financial Times* reported that partners, including **Oracle** [(ORCL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/orcl), **SoftBank** [(SFTBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sftby), **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv), **[Crusoe](https://www.tipranks.com/private-companies/crusoe)**, and **Blue Owl Capital** [(OBDC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/obdc), are [collectively taking on about $100 billion](https://www.tipranks.com/news/softbank-orcl-crwv-take-on-100b-debt-to-fuel-openais-growth-is-it-worth-the-risk) in debt to fund OpenAI’s massive infrastructure projects. Oracle’s stock fell 1.49% on the news, as investors grew wary of rising costs linked to AI data centers. Analysts noted that OpenAI’s strategy of “leveraging other balance sheets” could put pressure on partners even as the company expands globally.

Meanwhile, **GameStop** [(GME)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gme) made a surprise comeback, rising more than 3% after [Michael Burry](https://www.tipranks.com/experts/hedge-funds/michael-burry) shared old letters and emails from his time investing in the retailer. The nostalgic posts reignited chatter among retail traders, making GameStop one of the most mentioned tickers on social media. Still, analysts said the move had little to do with fundamentals.

**Intel** [(INTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/intc) was the standout among large-cap stocks, gaining over 10% for the week as investors welcomed signs of renewed strength in the chipmaker’s PC business. Other gainers included **Moderna** [(MRNA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mrna), **SanDisk** [(SNDK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sndk), and **Western Digital** [(WDC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wdc), each rising between 3% and 4%.

## **The Week Ahead**

Looking ahead, attention turns to the Federal Reserve’s December policy meeting, where traders now see an 80% chance of a quarter-point rate cut. Investors will also watch for November jobs data and updates from the manufacturing sector for clues on the strength of the economy heading into 2026.

With inflation cooling and borrowing costs easing, analysts expect continued support for equities into year-end. However, as the AI trade resets and market leadership shifts, volatility may stay elevated. For now, the market mood appears steady, with investors cautiously optimistic that the next Fed move could mark the start of a softer monetary path.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The [earnings calendar](https://www.tipranks.com/calendars/earnings) stays active this week, with software, cybersecurity, and retail names taking center stage as the final wave of November results rolls in.

On Tuesday, **Salesforce** [(CRM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crm) will headline after the close, with investors watching for updates on enterprise software demand and margins following steady growth in cloud revenue. **Snowflake** [(SNOW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/snow) will also report, with Wall Street focusing on consumption trends across data analytics workloads. Wednesday brings key reports from **CrowdStrike Holdings** [(CRWD)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwd), **Marvell Technology** [(MRVL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mrvl), and **Okta** [(OKTA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/okta), all offering a closer look at cybersecurity budgets and chip sector demand.

Later in the week, **MongoDB** [(MDB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mdb) and **Credo Technology Group** [(CRDO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crdo) will release earnings after the close. Both companies carry strong buy ratings, with analysts expecting continued growth in cloud database adoption and connectivity hardware demand. **Hewlett Packard Enterprise** [(HPE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpe) and **Ulta Beauty** [(ULTA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ulta) will follow on Thursday, giving the market a read on enterprise software spending, IT infrastructure, and consumer retail resilience.

Rounding out the week, **Toronto Dominion Bank** [(TD)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/td), **Kroger Company** [(KR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/kr), and **Dollar General** [(DG)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dg) will report before the open on Friday.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

A new week brings a broad lineup of dividend-paying companies across industries, from blue-chip tech to consumer goods and financials.

Starting the week, **Coca-Cola** [(KO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ko) and **McDonald’s** [(MCD)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mcd) will pay $0.51 and $1.86 per share. **Lockheed Martin** [(LMT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lmt) and **Northrop Grumman** [(NOC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/noc) will follow, paying shareholders $3.45 and $2.31 per share, as defense stocks continue to attract steady income investors.

In the materials and energy space, **Cameco** [(CCJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ccj) and **Agnico Eagle** [(AEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aem) will distribute $0.17 and $0.40, respectively, while Schlumberger [(SLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/slb) is set to pay $0.28 later in the week.

Among the financials, **Bank of America** [(BAC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bac) will pay $0.28 per share, while **Goldman Sachs Group** [(GS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gs) will follow with a $4.00 payout.

Tech investors will see dividends from **Nvidia** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) and **Qualcomm** (QCOM), which will pay $0.01 and $0.89 per share, respectively.

Consumer and retail names remain active, too. **Nike** [(NKE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nke) will pay $0.41 per share, while **PepsiCo** [(PEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pep) delivers $1.42 and **Union Pacific** [(UNP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/unp) returns $1.38 per share.

Finally, large-cap industrials like **Waste Management** [(WM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wm) and **Dominion Energy** [(D)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/d) will offer $0.82 and $0.67, respectively, while **BlackRock** [(BLK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/blk) will distribute a sizable $5.21 per share.

# Bears RB D'Andre Swift wins FedEx Ground Player of the Week

![Bears Wire](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/lfI5l1HsZMS4KwdDWqASXQ--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTIxNjtoPTU2O2NmPXdlYnA-/https://s.yimg.com/os/creatr-uploaded-images/2020-11/8bd69bd0-2b14-11eb-bfdf-bdeafc7a4bfc)
![Bears Wire](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/6nCYv6pO3XayM6pVSquyZA--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTIxNjtoPTU2O2NmPXdlYnA-/https://s.yimg.com/os/creatr-uploaded-images/2020-11/68102180-2b14-11eb-9bdf-1dc8a9ab45a7)
![](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/wD09M.q58CLOZq16kWxRmA--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTk2MDtoPTY3NztjZj13ZWJw/https://media.zenfs.com/en/chicago_bears_wire_usa_today_sports_articles_533/815bc036872e5696d9397c94c61e6a7e)

The [Chicago Bears](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/chicago-bears/326) ran all over the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/philadelphia-eagles/354) on Black Friday, winning 24-15, and one player is getting recognized for his efforts in the victory.

Running back D'Andre Swift has been named the FedEx Ground Player of the Week after he gashed the Eagles on Friday. Swift carried the ball 18 times for a season-high 125 yards and a touchdown. He was part of an outstanding tandem with rookie Kyle Monangai, who totaled 130 yards on 22 carries and a touchdown. Together, the duo rushed for 255 yards in one of the most dominant rushing performances in franchise history.

Swift, who has 774 rushing yards and five touchdowns in 11 games, is on pace for a career year in 2025 and has played a significant role in the Bears' 9-3 record. Chicago is atop the NFC going into Week 14 and is playing their best ball of the year as they look to make the postseason for the first time since 2020.

This is the first time Swift has won the FedEx Ground Player of the Week award and the first time a Bears player has won since Khalil Herbert in Week 16 of the 2023 season. Quarterback Caleb Williams won the FedEx Air Player of the Week back in Week 3 following his stellar performance against the Dallas Cowboys. The FedEx Air Player of the Week was [Green Bay Packers](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/green-bay-packers/335) quarterback Jordan Love, whom the Bears play this weekend.

*This article originally appeared on Bears Wire: [Bears RB D'Andre Swift wins FedEx Ground Player of the Week](https://bearswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/bears/2025/12/03/bears-dandre-swift-wins-fedex-ground-player-of-week/87593019007/)*

# FedEx launches global AI education programme for its workforce

## The training will focus on building common AI fluency and developing capabilities to apply the technology in day-to-day functions.

By[Our Correspondent

|4 Dec 2025 12:15 PM IST

FedEx has announced a global AI Education and Literacy programme aimed at equipping its workforce with skills to work with new technologies across its operations. The company said the initiative will provide personalised, role-based training for employees in all regions.

FedEx noted that the programme is part of its multi-year transformation plan in which it is adopting AI-powered tools to improve supply chain performance. The training will focus on building common AI fluency and developing capabilities to apply the technology in day-to-day functions.

“The future of business is being shaped by data and AI more than ever before,” said Raj Subramaniam, president and CEO, FedEx Corporation. "Our people remain at the heart of everything we do as FedEx continues its evolution into an AI-powered enterprise." We’re investing in AI education tools to help our team members grow their skills, support safer, smarter work, and unlock new opportunities across the business.”

FedEx has partnered with Accenture to design and deliver specialised AI training modules. Accenture will use its LearnVantage platform to create scalable programmes that include skill recognition and live sessions. The company said these modules will give employees personalised pathways to build AI literacy aligned with their roles and career goals.

The training will focus on creating a shared understanding of technology and responsible AI use across the organisation. FedEx said employees will gain the skills to apply AI within their functions, while leaders will receive guidance on integrating AI into team activities and wider processes.

“We are on a journey to empower our people with AI literacy and the practical technology skills needed to keep driving our business forward,” said Vishal Talwar, chief digital and information officer, FedEx Corporation. “As we create a shared, common understanding of AI internally at FedEx, team members will have access to modules, AI certifications, and mastery opportunities to help them grow in their careers.”

“FedEx is making supply chains smarter for everyone by putting its people at the centre and providing them with the training they need to thrive in the age of AI,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “We are excited to partner with FedEx to deliver role-based training that enables its employees to use AI responsibly, discover new ways of working, and confidently drive transformational change.”

_Accenture to support the company’s AI training needs with speed and scale._

MEMPHIS, Tenn. Dec. 2, 2025 – FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) today announced the launch of an enterprise-wide AI Education and Literacy program, which includes personalized, roles-based trainings for team members around the world. This program reinforces the company’s commitment to investing in the development of its people, consistent with its culture.

As part of a multi-year transformation journey, the company is using AI-powered solutions to make supply chains smarter for everyone. This AI Education and Literacy program will build common AI fluency and skills across the global FedEx enterprise, helping team members develop and enhance capabilities to apply AI responsibly and effectively.

“The future of business is being shaped by data and AI more than ever before,” said Raj Subramaniam, president and CEO, FedEx Corporation. “As FedEx continues its evolution into an AI-powered enterprise, our people remain at the heart of everything we do. We’re investing in AI education tools to help our team members grow their skills; support safer, smarter work; and unlock new opportunities across the business.”

In addition to building out internal training programs that expand on AI fundamentals, FedEx has tapped Accenture to provide customized AI education programs. Through its AI-native training platform LearnVantage, Accenture will provide tailored, scalable training, complete with skill recognition and interactive live training sessions to drive adoption. Personalized skilling pathways will also empower FedEx team members to build AI literacy depending on where they are on their professional growth journey.

The enhanced AI training offering is designed to create a shared language of technology understanding across the FedEx team. Employees will learn the skills they need to apply AI responsibly within their function. FedEx leaders will be equipped with the knowledge of how to embed AI into their own work, their teams’ work, and cross-functional processes to drive transformational change.

“We are on a journey to empower our people with AI literacy and the practical technology skills needed to keep driving our business forward,” said Vishal Talwar, chief digital and information officer, FedEx Corporation. “As we create a shared, common understanding of AI internally at FedEx, team members will have access to modules, AI certifications, and mastery opportunities to help grow in their careers.”

“FedEx is making supply chains smarter for everyone by putting its people at the center and providing them with the training they need to thrive in the age of AI,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “We are excited to partner with FedEx to deliver role-based training that enables its employees to use AI responsibly, discover new ways of working, and confidently drive transformational change. Together, we can help unlock the full value of AI across the company.”

FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce, and business services. With annual revenue of $89 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. # The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 30

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week higher as markets cheered signs of slower [inflation](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators/inflation-rate) and rising odds of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.54%, the Nasdaq **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** rose 0.78%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** added 0.61%. Treasury yields eased, with the 10-year note [closing at 4.00%.](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators)

Economic data showed cooling trends in both prices and growth. The inflation rate [stood at 3.01%](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), unemployment edged up to 4.40%, and real GDP growth came in at 3.80%. Retail sales rose a modest 0.07%, signaling that consumers are still spending, but at a slower pace. The Federal Funds Rate was 4.09%, down slightly from September.

In commodities, silver **[(XAGUSD)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:xagusd)** surged 6.49% to $57.09 per ounce, hitting record highs for the year. Gold **[(XAUUSD)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:xauusd)** rose 1.29%, while oil prices [slipped 0.29%](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl) to $58.48 a barrel. Natural gas jumped 6.67%, reflecting colder weather forecasts and strong export demand.

## **Big Tech Takes a Breather**

The story of the week was the pullback in major technology names after a strong year of gains. **Nvidia** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) fell 1.81%, its worst month since 2022, as investors rotated away from high-growth stocks. The decline followed reports that **Meta Platforms** [(META)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/meta) may buy [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) chips from **Alphabet** [(GOOGL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/googl) instead of Nvidia, sparking talk that Nvidia’s market dominance could face its first real test.

Meanwhile, Alphabet climbed 13.8% for the month after revealing its upgraded Gemini 3 AI model and a potential new chip deal with Meta. **Broadcom** [(AVGO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/avgo) also gained 7.6% on expectations it will benefit from demand tied to Google’s AI projects. However, investors grew more selective, with many looking to take profits from names that led the 2025 rally.

The rotation weighed on the broader AI trade, but it also reflected healthy rebalancing. Analysts said investors are adjusting to the idea that AI spending growth may spread to more firms and chip designs. The shift helped steady markets as traders prepared for what some call a “Santa Claus rally” fueled by rate-cut expectations.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

Defense startup **Anduril** grabbed headlines after a *Wall Street Journal* report said its autonomous drone systems failed multiple field tests. The company, founded by Palmer Luckey and backed by Peter Thiel, said the issues were part of its “fail fast” approach to innovation. Still, the news raised fresh questions about the reliability of AI weapons systems in active use.

Another major story centered on **OpenAI’s** financing model. *The Financial Times* reported that partners, including **Oracle** [(ORCL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/orcl), **SoftBank** [(SFTBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sftby), **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv), **[Crusoe](https://www.tipranks.com/private-companies/crusoe)**, and **Blue Owl Capital** [(OBDC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/obdc), are [collectively taking on about $100 billion](https://www.tipranks.com/news/softbank-orcl-crwv-take-on-100b-debt-to-fuel-openais-growth-is-it-worth-the-risk) in debt to fund OpenAI’s massive infrastructure projects. Oracle’s stock fell 1.49% on the news, as investors grew wary of rising costs linked to AI data centers. Analysts noted that OpenAI’s strategy of “leveraging other balance sheets” could put pressure on partners even as the company expands globally.

Meanwhile, **GameStop** [(GME)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gme) made a surprise comeback, rising more than 3% after [Michael Burry](https://www.tipranks.com/experts/hedge-funds/michael-burry) shared old letters and emails from his time investing in the retailer. The nostalgic posts reignited chatter among retail traders, making GameStop one of the most mentioned tickers on social media. Still, analysts said the move had little to do with fundamentals.

**Intel** [(INTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/intc) was the standout among large-cap stocks, gaining over 10% for the week as investors welcomed signs of renewed strength in the chipmaker’s PC business. Other gainers included **Moderna** [(MRNA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mrna), **SanDisk** [(SNDK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sndk), and **Western Digital** [(WDC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wdc), each rising between 3% and 4%.

## **The Week Ahead**

Looking ahead, attention turns to the Federal Reserve’s December policy meeting, where traders now see an 80% chance of a quarter-point rate cut. Investors will also watch for November jobs data and updates from the manufacturing sector for clues on the strength of the economy heading into 2026.

With inflation cooling and borrowing costs easing, analysts expect continued support for equities into year-end. However, as the AI trade resets and market leadership shifts, volatility may stay elevated. For now, the market mood appears steady, with investors cautiously optimistic that the next Fed move could mark the start of a softer monetary path.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The [earnings calendar](https://www.tipranks.com/calendars/earnings) stays active this week, with software, cybersecurity, and retail names taking center stage as the final wave of November results rolls in.

On Tuesday, **Salesforce** [(CRM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crm) will headline after the close, with investors watching for updates on enterprise software demand and margins following steady growth in cloud revenue. **Snowflake** [(SNOW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/snow) will also report, with Wall Street focusing on consumption trends across data analytics workloads. Wednesday brings key reports from **CrowdStrike Holdings** [(CRWD)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwd), **Marvell Technology** [(MRVL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mrvl), and **Okta** [(OKTA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/okta), all offering a closer look at cybersecurity budgets and chip sector demand.

Later in the week, **MongoDB** [(MDB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mdb) and **Credo Technology Group** [(CRDO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crdo) will release earnings after the close. Both companies carry strong buy ratings, with analysts expecting continued growth in cloud database adoption and connectivity hardware demand. **Hewlett Packard Enterprise** [(HPE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpe) and **Ulta Beauty** [(ULTA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ulta) will follow on Thursday, giving the market a read on enterprise software spending, IT infrastructure, and consumer retail resilience.

Rounding out the week, **Toronto Dominion Bank** [(TD)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/td), **Kroger Company** [(KR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/kr), and **Dollar General** [(DG)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dg) will report before the open on Friday.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

A new week brings a broad lineup of dividend-paying companies across industries, from blue-chip tech to consumer goods and financials.

Starting the week, **Coca-Cola** [(KO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ko) and **McDonald’s** [(MCD)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mcd) will pay $0.51 and $1.86 per share. **Lockheed Martin** [(LMT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lmt) and **Northrop Grumman** [(NOC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/noc) will follow, paying shareholders $3.45 and $2.31 per share, as defense stocks continue to attract steady income investors.

In the materials and energy space, **Cameco** [(CCJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ccj) and **Agnico Eagle** [(AEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aem) will distribute $0.17 and $0.40, respectively, while Schlumberger [(SLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/slb) is set to pay $0.28 later in the week.

Among the financials, **Bank of America** [(BAC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bac) will pay $0.28 per share, while **Goldman Sachs Group** [(GS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gs) will follow with a $4.00 payout.

Tech investors will see dividends from **Nvidia** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) and **Qualcomm** (QCOM), which will pay $0.01 and $0.89 per share, respectively.

Consumer and retail names remain active, too. **Nike** [(NKE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nke) will pay $0.41 per share, while **PepsiCo** [(PEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pep) delivers $1.42 and **Union Pacific** [(UNP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/unp) returns $1.38 per share.

Finally, large-cap industrials like **Waste Management** [(WM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wm) and **Dominion Energy** [(D)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/d) will offer $0.82 and $0.67, respectively, while **BlackRock** [(BLK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/blk) will distribute a sizable $5.21 per share.

# Bears RB D'Andre Swift wins FedEx Ground Player of the Week

![Bears Wire](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/lfI5l1HsZMS4KwdDWqASXQ--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTIxNjtoPTU2O2NmPXdlYnA-/https://s.yimg.com/os/creatr-uploaded-images/2020-11/8bd69bd0-2b14-11eb-bfdf-bdeafc7a4bfc)
![Bears Wire](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/6nCYv6pO3XayM6pVSquyZA--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTIxNjtoPTU2O2NmPXdlYnA-/https://s.yimg.com/os/creatr-uploaded-images/2020-11/68102180-2b14-11eb-9bdf-1dc8a9ab45a7)
![](https://s.yimg.com/ny/api/res/1.2/wD09M.q58CLOZq16kWxRmA--/YXBwaWQ9aGlnaGxhbmRlcjt3PTk2MDtoPTY3NztjZj13ZWJw/https://media.zenfs.com/en/chicago_bears_wire_usa_today_sports_articles_533/815bc036872e5696d9397c94c61e6a7e)

The [Chicago Bears](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/chicago-bears/326) ran all over the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/philadelphia-eagles/354) on Black Friday, winning 24-15, and one player is getting recognized for his efforts in the victory.

Running back D'Andre Swift has been named the FedEx Ground Player of the Week after he gashed the Eagles on Friday. Swift carried the ball 18 times for a season-high 125 yards and a touchdown. He was part of an outstanding tandem with rookie Kyle Monangai, who totaled 130 yards on 22 carries and a touchdown. Together, the duo rushed for 255 yards in one of the most dominant rushing performances in franchise history.

Swift, who has 774 rushing yards and five touchdowns in 11 games, is on pace for a career year in 2025 and has played a significant role in the Bears' 9-3 record. Chicago is atop the NFC going into Week 14 and is playing their best ball of the year as they look to make the postseason for the first time since 2020.

This is the first time Swift has won the FedEx Ground Player of the Week award and the first time a Bears player has won since Khalil Herbert in Week 16 of the 2023 season. Quarterback Caleb Williams won the FedEx Air Player of the Week back in Week 3 following his stellar performance against the Dallas Cowboys. The FedEx Air Player of the Week was [Green Bay Packers](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/green-bay-packers/335) quarterback Jordan Love, whom the Bears play this weekend.

# FedEx launches global AI education programme for its workforce

## The training will focus on building common AI fluency and developing capabilities to apply the technology in day-to-day functions.

By[Our Correspondent

|4 Dec 2025 12:15 PM IST

FedEx has announced a global AI Education and Literacy programme aimed at equipping its workforce with skills to work with new technologies across its operations. The company said the initiative will provide personalised, role-based training for employees in all regions.

FedEx noted that the programme is part of its multi-year transformation plan in which it is adopting AI-powered tools to improve supply chain performance. The training will focus on building common AI fluency and developing capabilities to apply the technology in day-to-day functions.

“The future of business is being shaped by data and AI more than ever before,” said Raj Subramaniam, president and CEO, FedEx Corporation. "Our people remain at the heart of everything we do as FedEx continues its evolution into an AI-powered enterprise." We’re investing in AI education tools to help our team members grow their skills, support safer, smarter work, and unlock new opportunities across the business.”

FedEx has partnered with Accenture to design and deliver specialised AI training modules. Accenture will use its LearnVantage platform to create scalable programmes that include skill recognition and live sessions. The company said these modules will give employees personalised pathways to build AI literacy aligned with their roles and career goals.

The training will focus on creating a shared understanding of technology and responsible AI use across the organisation. FedEx said employees will gain the skills to apply AI within their functions, while leaders will receive guidance on integrating AI into team activities and wider processes.

“We are on a journey to empower our people with AI literacy and the practical technology skills needed to keep driving our business forward,” said Vishal Talwar, chief digital and information officer, FedEx Corporation. “As we create a shared, common understanding of AI internally at FedEx, team members will have access to modules, AI certifications, and mastery opportunities to help them grow in their careers.”

“FedEx is making supply chains smarter for everyone by putting its people at the centre and providing them with the training they need to thrive in the age of AI,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “We are excited to partner with FedEx to deliver role-based training that enables its employees to use AI responsibly, discover new ways of working, and confidently drive transformational change.”

**FedEx Empowers Global Workforce with AI Education and Literacy Program**
==========================================================================

_Accenture to support the company’s AI training needs with speed and scale._

MEMPHIS, Tenn. Dec. 2, 2025 – FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) today announced the launch of an enterprise-wide AI Education and Literacy program, which includes personalized, roles-based trainings for team members around the world. This program reinforces the company’s commitment to investing in the development of its people, consistent with its culture.

As part of a multi-year transformation journey, the company is using AI-powered solutions to make supply chains smarter for everyone. This AI Education and Literacy program will build common AI fluency and skills across the global FedEx enterprise, helping team members develop and enhance capabilities to apply AI responsibly and effectively.

“The future of business is being shaped by data and AI more than ever before,” said Raj Subramaniam, president and CEO, FedEx Corporation. “As FedEx continues its evolution into an AI-powered enterprise, our people remain at the heart of everything we do. We’re investing in AI education tools to help our team members grow their skills; support safer, smarter work; and unlock new opportunities across the business.”

In addition to building out internal training programs that expand on AI fundamentals, FedEx has tapped Accenture to provide customized AI education programs. Through its AI-native training platform LearnVantage, Accenture will provide tailored, scalable training, complete with skill recognition and interactive live training sessions to drive adoption. Personalized skilling pathways will also empower FedEx team members to build AI literacy depending on where they are on their professional growth journey.

The enhanced AI training offering is designed to create a shared language of technology understanding across the FedEx team. Employees will learn the skills they need to apply AI responsibly within their function. FedEx leaders will be equipped with the knowledge of how to embed AI into their own work, their teams’ work, and cross-functional processes to drive transformational change.

“We are on a journey to empower our people with AI literacy and the practical technology skills needed to keep driving our business forward,” said Vishal Talwar, chief digital and information officer, FedEx Corporation. “As we create a shared, common understanding of AI internally at FedEx, team members will have access to modules, AI certifications, and mastery opportunities to help grow in their careers.”

“FedEx is making supply chains smarter for everyone by putting its people at the center and providing them with the training they need to thrive in the age of AI,” said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. “We are excited to partner with FedEx to deliver role-based training that enables its employees to use AI responsibly, discover new ways of working, and confidently drive transformational change. Together, we can help unlock the full value of AI across the company.”

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 30

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week higher as markets cheered signs of slower [inflation](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators/inflation-rate) and rising odds of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.54%, the Nasdaq **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** rose 0.78%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** added 0.61%. Treasury yields eased, with the 10-year note [closing at 4.00%.](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators)

### TipRanks Black Friday Sale

* [Claim 60% off TipRanks Premium](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-premium/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  for the data-backed insights and research tools you need to invest with confidence.
